description:
LANDED 29b07acfa on wt/kdt13-boundaries (2026-09-02; parent 8c3d5ce90 =
stage B; one commit, 18 files +549/-119). Refuter FIX-THEN-MERGE, seven
findings folded before merge. Coordinator gate COORD-GATE-1788390985:
fmt clean, release build 0 warnings, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo
test --lib 1586/0/5, fixture_matrix --test-threads=1 485/0/9 (known-red
names unchanged), the three behaviour fixtures byte-equal to expected on
interp, JIT and AOT.

WHAT LANDED. ClosureLit.fn_id is Option<FnId>; None is the ANONYMOUS
literal: a closure of some function over exactly these capture types,
printed `closure[?](int)`. Types::erase_transported_closure_identities
(the only minter of anonymous literals; its only caller is
World::canonical_activation_key) erases the BRAND and keeps capture
types recursively (brands inside captured closures erased too, so
same-typed literals share one forwarder body). A capture-free literal
still erases to the bare arrow (nothing left to say; keeps the fz-6gb
ladder sharing exactly: 32-site zero-capture ladder 59 -> 59 executables,
32-site same-typed int-capture ladder 59 -> 59). A forwarder receiving
one lambda at int and float captures gets one body per capture type,
each callsite one grounded target: same_lambda_two_capture_types.fz has
`P.run/2[closure[?](float), int]` / `[closure[?](int), int]` and ZERO
dispatch nodes (base: one run body, a two-arm dispatch); job spans
336 -> 321. The dynamic twin stays green and GAINS the stage-B question
at main's callsite (the first moment it needs one) -- the corrected
acceptance, measured.

WHY A AND B COMPOSE (corrected by the refuter; the first landing named
a projection guard that was dead code, 0 hits over 597 fixtures + the
suite): the KEYING rule. An anonymous literal is written only into
ActivationKey.arrow, only in slots the DispatchMask marks Ignore, only
for a non-recursive body that does not consume callable identity; a
runtime test is projected from a callsite's surface_inputs (value
evidence). The two never meet, so an anonymous literal cannot reach a
dispatch predicate. Pinned from the keying side
(the_forwarder_erasure_anonymises_only_the_slots_no_test_reads) and
stated once at the single arrival site (debug_assert; release keeps the
sound CallableShapes::any()).

DELETED (grep-proven): Descr::without_closure_lits (last caller gone);
the dead anonymous guard in runtime_type_predicate_callables; every
comment/doc stating the forwarder key keeps only arity; the
`fnref[?]` implication in canon.rs/format.rs (a fnref has no captures,
so it erases whole); erase_closure_identity_preserves_callable_surface_
shape (pinned nothing) rewritten as ..._drops_the_brand_and_keeps_the_
captures. Re-homed: the runtime-question and capture-unpack gates onto
the dynamic twin (the static fixture no longer asks or unpacks);
..._is_the_static_key pins the zero-dispatch law.

EMPTINESS (refuter F2): func_clause_empty now calls a clause empty when a
positive literal's own capture type is empty -- anon(int) ∩ L(float) is
empty (it had intersected to a literal over `none` reported inhabited);
the same line closes the pre-existing same-brand hole L(int) ∩ L(float).
Law stated in set-theoretic-types.md.

CONTAINMENT WITNESS (refuter F4, fz-kdt.171 folded and closed):
callable_union_capture_containment.fz had gone fully static under the
new keys (1 -> 0 dispatch nodes) and 171's own reproducer did not
reproduce; re-homed on the dynamic any-vs-float shape: correct on three
doors, and under an overlap swap of CallableShapes::enumerates interp
prints 12.0 and JIT/AOT abort in fz_closure_get_capture_f64.

MOVEMENT (597 fixtures x 3 doors, base vs head): 0 behaviour movers; 58
canon movers: 45 key-text only, 13 gain executables / 0 lose, five lose
dispatch nodes, four gain ten; net -52 runtime questions corpus-wide.
Same-lambda capture-type split (this ticket's purpose): 6. Different-
lambda capture-tuple split (a capture-free lambda keyed apart from a
capture-bearing one at one forwarder; on the minimal pair +1 executable
-1 runtime test; in five of seven programs no test removed): 8 files /
7 programs -- fz-kdt.169. Inventory and ANALYSIS_CLAIM_RATCHET pins
re-pinned with cause. Stress lens 812 comparisons: 0 movers; FIFO/LIFO
mover set unchanged (00277, dead_closure_capture_empty_list);
double-compile byte-identical; wall clock max 0.44s.

TICKETS FROM THE ROUND: fz-kdt.169 (the different-lambda split grain),
fz-kdt.172 (dnf-hygiene tests cover zero-capture literals only),
fz-kdt.173 (anonymous+branded union would be dropped by
callable_value_clauses; unreachable, unstated), fz-kdt.174 (00277
compiled to two different backend programs across sessions from one
binary -- pre-existing schedule dependence, the FIFO/LIFO mover).

PREMISE CORRECTED by the fz-kdt.127.1 build (commit f34c2aaa3, base
172ab21f1). The cold review's probe table says sl3dyn under (B) alone
gets "run's callsite, shape test". MEASURED FALSE, both dynamic variants,
head canon byte-identical to base's:

  fixtures2/behavior/same_lambda_two_capture_types_dynamic.fz (mailbox
    scrutinee)  -- `diff` of the backend dumps: no difference at all.
  review/probes/sl3dyn.fz (Process.heap_alloc_stats scrutinee) -- same.

There is no headB/sl3dyn.canon among the review's artifacts (only headA
and headAB), so the row was inferred from A+B rather than measured on B.

WHY it is right that nothing moved, and what it means here. `P.run/2` and
`P.twice/2` are each ONE body over the union
`closure[mk#L](int) | closure[mk#L](float)`, and `twice` calls `f`
INDIRECTLY -- `closure_call ... target=-`. The value's own word selects
the construction wrapper and the wrapper's member selection answers for
the capture layout. No callsite has two targets, so no callsite asks. The
program is correct at base for exactly that reason, and stage (B) has
nothing to add to it.

So this fixture's role in this epic is precisely and only the one the
review's finding F2 gave it: it is the GUARD for THIS ticket. Stage (A)
splits `run` by capture type, main's callsite becomes a 2-target dispatch
in fz-kdt.127's shape, and that is the first moment the dynamic witness
needs the construction axis. This ticket's acceptance should therefore
read: the dynamic fixture stays green AND main's callsite gains a
construction-shape question (`s0 type(closure[P.mk/1#lambda](int))` or
its float twin) -- which is a NEW canon mover for stage (A), not a fact
already true.

Everything else this ticket depends on is in place: an anonymous closure
literal projects to `CallableShapes::any()` (the compose guard), the
capture unpack is keyed on the minting constructions rather than the
function, and the callable axis is PerPosition with containment
admission.

BUILT, one commit 1d7943335 on wt/kdt127-2-build (base 8c3d5ce90), 14 files
+~330/-~90. NOT closed.

REPRESENTATION: `ClosureLit.fn_id: Option<FnId>`, `None` = the ANONYMOUS
literal (a closure of SOME function over exactly these capture types). Chosen
over a distinct lit-less-with-captures form because the anonymous literal is the
same thing a branded one is minus a field: every reader already reads
kind/fn_id/captures together, derived Eq/Hash and `refine_widen`'s fn_id
equality say the right thing about `None` for free, and only the sites that
must DECIDE (emptiness, meet, order, canon, format, callable_clauses,
runtime_type_predicate_callables, callable_identity_targets, closure_lit_parts)
take a three-line match with the brand law beside them. Two deliberate rules:
a capture-free literal still erases to the bare arrow (nothing left to say --
minting `closure[?]()` would split every zero-capture lambda away from the
plain-arrow surface the fz-6gb ladder shares), and an anonymous literal reaches
CallableShapes::any() (stage B's compose seam).

F1 -- THE COMPOSE SEAM WAS DEAD CODE AND THE STATED MECHANISM WAS WRONG.
The inner anonymous guard in `runtime_type_predicate_callables`
(types/mod.rs:1451-1456) is deleted: `callable_identity_targets`, which this
same commit changed to `.collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?`, already returns None on
any anonymous literal, so the inner guard could never be reached. The site now
reads `lit.fn_id.expect("callable_identity_targets refused every anonymous
literal")`.

The CORRECT statement, now in `callable_identity_targets`'s doc and in the
commit message: what makes stage A's erased key and stage B's construction axis
compose is the KEYING rule, not a projection. An anonymous literal is minted in
exactly ONE place -- `Types::erase_transported_closure_identities`
(types/mod.rs:874), whose one non-test caller is
`World::canonical_activation_key` (world.rs:1877) -- and it goes only into
`ActivationKey.arrow`, only into slots the dispatch mask marks
`DispatchDemand::Ignore`, only for a non-recursive body with
`consumes_callable_identity == false`. A runtime test is projected from a
VALUE's type: `callsite_dispatch::runtime_questions` (callsite_dispatch.rs:381)
reads `CallTargetSummary::surface_inputs`, the callsite's own argument evidence.
The two never meet. Measured: the anonymous arms of both functions fire 0 times
over 597 fixtures, 0 with `--dump backend=`, and 0 over the whole
`cargo test --lib`.

ONE gate keeps it honest: a `debug_assert!` at that single arrival site, whose
message states the invariant; release still takes the sound `?` ->
`CallableShapes::any()` fallback. Pinned from the KEYING side by a new unit
test, `the_forwarder_erasure_anonymises_only_the_slots_no_test_reads`: erase an
arrow under mask [Ignore, Whole]; slot 0 loses its brand and renders `#?`, slot
1 comes back byte-identical to the branded input and still projects to a
`CallableShape` naming its construction.

Prose corrected in place, not layered: types/mod.rs:1440, this ticket's
description, fz-kdt.127's description, and the commit-message paragraph.
semantic-fixpoint.md never stated the wrong mechanism (0 hits for "compose" /
"CallableShapes::any" across .agent/docs). Note for the record: this ticket's
2026-09-02T20:24 comment and fz-kdt.127.1's ledger both call the projection
"the compose guard" -- those are historical and are superseded by this comment.

F2 -- ANONYMOUS MEET EMPTINESS HOLE CLOSED. `func_clause_empty`
(emptiness.rs:199) now calls a clause empty when any positive literal's own
capture type is empty. A closure holds exactly one value per capture slot, so
`#4closure[none]` denotes nothing. The anonymous literal reaches it by MERGING
with a branded one (it is every brand at once, so `PosMeet` no longer reports
Distinct and the merged capture is `int & float`); one brand at two capture
types reaches it the same way, which is the hole that predates this commit --
the one line closes both.

and this head binary over the SAME (head) corpus, 597 `.fz` / 469 backend dumps
("dispatch node" = a `dispatch miss=` or `tail dispatch inputs=` line):

    same_lambda_two_capture_types_dynamic 2->6,
    callable_union_capture_containment 1->3.

lose ... two gain" and contradicted it -- both now read the measured five/four.
The refuter's two extra losers were the containment fixture (rehomed by this

F4 -- fz-kdt.171 FOLDED AND CLOSED. See that ticket for the full measurement:
the fixture is rehomed on the dynamic `any`-vs-`float` shape, correct on three
doors (DOORS-1788389883), and RED on three doors under the fz-kdt.167 overlap

F6 -- `fnref[?]` implication removed from canon.rs and format.rs. There was no
